ruleset.digest_algorithm: SHA-256 over ordered UTF-8 relative-path + NUL + raw-file-bytes

Cloud_Network_Completeness.detail: Azure has no exact Region; SAP and both partner-hosted boundaries have TBD locations. Ratio includes the 0.25 subcategory weight.
All four Azure satellite components lack an explicit VNET and Subnet or a clear SaaS endpoint classification. Ratio includes the 0.25 subcategory weight.
Owner labels are present, although SAP and Azure owner names remain TBD.
No duplicate infrastructure boundary was detected.

Connectivity.detail: Only 11 cross-boundary arrows state 'IPsec private WAN'; no separate DC/cloud-level links identify MPLS, ExpressRoute, or an approved equivalent.
Every cross-boundary arrow carries TLS, SNC, IPsec, or SSH wording, subject to the unresolved approvals called out in the blueprint.

Technical_Component_Completeness.detail: Thirty-seven generic component boxes do not visibly state a component category; ratio includes the 0.333 subcategory weight.
All eight custom-developed components show a language/framework string, though versions remain TBD.
The PNG has no K8s/VM/platform runtime frames or visible runtime labels; draw.io tooltips and blueprint-only metadata do not make the exported view self-contained.

Interaction_Integration.detail: SYS-06 -> SYS-41 points away from Kafka although the rule requires both producer and consumer relations to point to Kafka.
No bidirectional edge style was detected.
Protocol names are present, but all 80 arrows omit the explicit port required by input/prompt.md; ratio includes the 0.25 subcategory weight.
Ten SSOC-to-SAP calls go directly from SYS-07..SYS-11 to SYS-20/SYS-24 rather than through SYS-05 or another approved mediator; ratio includes the 0.25 subcategory weight.

Security_Compliance.detail: Auth text exists on 80/80 arrows, but one of two Internet ingress routes bypasses F5 and two of ten data stores lack an explicit DB segment; normalized across S-001/S-002/S-003.
The user actor is disconnected from ADFS, Enterprise ID has no application callback, and AuthZ Platform is absent from the diagram; category deduction capped at its 0.333 weight.
The non-K8s vault remains unspecified and eight known CN-US application/event flows omit data classification and legal basis; category deduction capped at its 0.333 weight.

Terminology_Expression.detail: Thirty-seven physical components and nine physical zones use dashed borders contrary to V-001.
A legend exists but does not explain communication lines, ownership/status warning marker, or all boundary/line semantics.
Four dense regions have label-to-label, label-to-node, and edge-to-node overlap: CN primary Intranet, CN primary DB Zone, CN-to-secondary/SAP fan-out, and partner/MFT fan-out.
No prohibited VPC/VNET/Region terminology is used inside the private-DC boundaries.

issues.subject: Rendered PNG readability
issues.evidence: Four visually confirmed congestion regions obscure labels, arrow association, nodes, and zone boundaries; the CN primary Intranet/DB area is not reliably traceable.

issues.subject: 46 physical entities rendered with dashed borders
issues.evidence: The draw.io XML contains dashed=1 on 37 component nodes and 9 zone nodes, although these are physical deployment entities.

issues.subject: Azure US boundary
issues.evidence: The boundary title states 'exact region TBD'.

issues.subject: SAP and 3PL/file partner boundaries
issues.evidence: SAP location is TBD and both partner-hosted boundaries state locations TBD, affecting SYS-20..SYS-24 and SYS-42..SYS-50.

issues.subject: SYS-38 through SYS-41 Azure placement
issues.evidence: No VNET, Subnet, Private Endpoint, or explicit SaaS public/private endpoint classification is visible for any of the four components.

issues.subject: 26 of 37 cross-boundary arrows
issues.evidence: Only 11 cross-boundary arrows identify 'IPsec private WAN'; the remaining 26 do not identify the underlying connection type.

issues.subject: Private-DC and Azure interconnects
issues.evidence: Private WAN/IPsec is shown per application edge, but MPLS/equivalent DC links and ExpressRoute/equivalent Azure private connectivity are not shown as approved infrastructure links.

issues.subject: 37 of 52 technical components
issues.evidence: Generic boxes provide names and ownership colors but no visible component category; only 15 components convey category through specialized shape/legend semantics.

issues.subject: 52 of 52 technical components
issues.evidence: Runtime exists only in blueprint/tooltips; the exported PNG contains no K8s/VM/platform frames or visible runtime label.

issues.subject: 80 of 80 communication arrows
issues.evidence: Every edge omits an explicit port, violating input/prompt.md line 44 even though protocol and auth text are present.

issues.subject: SYS-06 -> SYS-41
issues.evidence: The consumer relation points away from Kafka; W-001/V-003 requires the SYS-41 consumer arrow to point toward SYS-06 Kafka.

issues.subject: 10 direct SSOC-to-SAP interactions
issues.evidence: SYS-07..SYS-11 connect directly to SYS-20 and SYS-24 instead of traversing SYS-05 or another approved integration node.

issues.subject: Internet -> SYS-30 Enterprise ID
issues.evidence: SYS-30 is drawn inside US DC Intranet and receives Internet traffic directly, bypassing F5/DMZ. Partner inbound paths to the application are not shown through F5.

issues.subject: Internal user authentication
issues.evidence: The User actor is disconnected. SYS-04 -> SYS-29 is shown, but the required user/front-end authentication path is not traceable from the actor to ADFS.

issues.subject: External user authentication
issues.evidence: Internet -> SYS-30 is present, but the application callback/entry point is absent and remains TBD in the blueprint, so Enterprise ID is not connected to the protected application flow.

issues.subject: AuthZ Platform
issues.evidence: The blueprint mentions AuthZ Platform and application RBAC, but no authorization node, connection, or visible RBAC/ABAC annotation exists in the PNG.

issues.subject: Credential protection
issues.evidence: Kubernetes Secrets appear in DB edge labels, but the enterprise vault for F5, WSO2, Kafka, data platforms, MFT platform, and network devices is unnamed and still blocked by TBD-009; no vault node or consumer connections are shown.

issues.subject: Eight known CN-US application/event flows
issues.evidence: Four flows to US DC/Azure SaaS applications plus four Azure application/event flows carry Acme Confidential data without field classification, minimization annotation, or applicable transfer basis.

issues.subject: Operational access
issues.evidence: The blueprint declares a PAW path, but the PNG has no Office Network, PAW, management plane, MFA/JIT path, or target-zone admin edges.

issues.subject: SYS-24 and SYS-33 data stores
issues.evidence: SYS-24 stored data is in an undifferentiated SAP Private Zone and SYS-33 lakehouse is in generic Intranet; neither has an explicit DB/data segment or equivalent internal isolation boundary.

issues.subject: Diagram legend
issues.evidence: The legend does not define arrow direction/line style, warning markers, status semantics, or all network-boundary styles used in the diagram.

issues.subject: Unapproved authentication assumptions
issues.evidence: mTLS for F5-to-nginx and 3PL APIs, SAP Logon Ticket/SNC endpoints, and the external callback are rendered as selected controls while blueprint TBD-004/TBD-005/TBD-006 remain unresolved.

issues.subject: Ten data-store nodes
issues.evidence: AES-256 appears only in blueprint/tooltips and is not visible on the data-store shapes in the exported PNG.

issues.subject: Azure child boundaries
issues.evidence: The Azure boundary uses an Azure shape, but its two child groups use AWS group/VPC-subnet symbols in the draw.io XML.

coverage_gaps: Business ownership and purpose are not visible in the diagram.
Security controls are described in the blueprint but key controls are absent from the PNG.
Governance approvals and cross-border legal basis remain TBD.
The mandatory PAW operational-access view is absent.

summary.evaluation: BLOCK-quality validation result: the rendered view is too congested to trace reliably and omits mandatory connectivity, runtime, authorization, secrets, PAW, and data-governance evidence. F5 ingress is only partially compliant, SAP calls bypass mediation, and several location/network-boundary facts remain TBD.
